To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a 14 kilo‐dalton cytosolic stimulatory protein has been purified from bovine cortex, and the protein has been shown to act as a stimulatory regulator for the Mg2+-independent Ca2+-ATPase of goat spermatozoa.
a low molecular mass cytosolic protein, purified from bovine cerebral cortex, can stimulate the Mg2+ independent form of goat sperm microsomes Ca2+‐dependent ATPase.
a low molecular mass cytosolic protein isolated from bovine brain stimulates the Mg2+ independent Ca2+-ATPase from goat sperm microsomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization from brain cytosol of a protein capable of regulating a Mg2+‐ independent Ca2+‐pump, a novel enzyme with potential physiological significance.
the isolation, purification and biochemical characterization of a protein which acts as an endogenous activator of a Mg2+‐ independent Ca2+‐ ATPase.
the isolation and characterization of a protein from the bovine brain that can act as an activator for the Mg2+-independent Ca2+-ATPase of the goat sperm microsomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein is a specific stimulator of Mg2+ independent Ca2+‐dependent ATPase.
the 14 kilodaltons cytosolic protein is an activator of the goat sperm Mg2+‐free Ca2+‐pump.
the protein is a low molecular mass endogenous stimulator for the Mg2+-independent Ca2+-ATPase from bovine brain microsomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this protein can act as an allosteric activator of the goat sperm Mg2+‐ independent Ca2+‐transport ATPase.
this protein acts as a stimulator of the Mg2+independent Ca2+-ATPase of goat sperm microsomes.
the 14 kD protein is an endogenous activator of the goat sperm microsomes Ca2+‐transport ATPase, which is distinct from the Ca2+‐dependent activator protein of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stimulator is a specific regulator of the Mg2+ ‐independent Ca2‐ATPase and is not a regulator of the SERCA type Ca2+ pumps.
the low molecular mass protein identified and characterized in the present study can serve as a potential regulator of the Mg2+ ‐independent Ca2 +‐ATPase in sperm and other cell types.
the Mg2+ independent Ca2+ ATPase is regulated by a low molecular weight protein, and the stimulatory effect of this protein is specific to the Mg2+ ‐independent form of Ca2+ ATPases.
